title: Digital Democracy Edinburgh: key dates
content:
Dear friend,

If you’re planning to join us for the forthcoming conference Digital Democracy Edinburgh, here are all the dates you need to know.

Perhaps you’d like to propose a session; or maybe you prefer to be in the audience. Either way,  we hope this timeline is useful.

You can register now for the conference, which will take place in the Edinburgh Futures Institute on 11 & 12 March 2027.

Over two days, it will bring together 150-200 leading practitioners, researchers, and policymakers to explore how digital tools can deepen participation and make democratic systems more effective and inclusive. Will you be one of them?

Places are limited, so book your ticket now.

Have you got something to add to the conference's core theme of technology to reimagine democratic decision-making and build a more resilient democracy for the future?

Digital Democracy Edinburgh provides opportunities for researchers, practitioners and others to contribute to the programme via the open call for proposals.

Please submit your proposal before 15 November. We look forward to reading it!

title: Links, the bumper edition
content:
Dear friend,

For many years, when we put together these emails we included a handful of links at the end, sharing the news articles that had caught our attention that month.

The “What we're reading” section has somewhat fallen by the wayside, but we know you liked it — you told us so. We’re thinking we might just bring it back now and again.

In return, we’d love to have a recommendation from you. What are you reading, listening to or watching?

Share a link with us to your favourite podcast, news source, blog or something else you think we might enjoy. Bonus points if it touches on our broad interest areas of democracy, transparency, community, climate action, data, or civic tech generally — but honestly, we’re open to all suggestions, and we’d love to hear about something outside our habitual bubble.

title: FOI reform in Germany and Mexico
content:
Dear friend,

We can’t take our Freedom of Information laws for granted — as we’ve seen through the years with governmental pushback both in the UK, and in countless countries around the world.

In this free webinar, we’ll hear from those at the frontline of defending the right to know in Germany and Mexico, two countries where recent changes have raised important questions about the future of Access to Information.

In Germany, FragDenStaat say that they are facing "the most serious attack on transparency in the history of the Federal Republic and a threat to our democracy", with a proposed scrapping of ATI. In Mexico, a change in the agency responsible for FOI has undermined public access to information, ruling against most requests.

We hope you’ll join us on Oct 26 to hear these fascinating stories, and what civil society is doing to kick back against such challenges: find out more and book here.

Veza is Strategic Campaigner at FragDenStaat (Ask the State) in Germany.

Like mySociety's WhatDoTheyKnow, FragDenStaat provides a simple way for citizens to submit FOI requests online; and they also campaign very actively around information rights.

title: Hear from the FOI regulators
content:
Dear friend,

For any country with an FOI regime, oversight is vital — otherwise, there’s nowhere for people to turn when the system fails.

In the UK we have the ICO, the Information Commissioner's Office; and there are regulatory authorities in many different forms in countries around the world.

But what do regulators do? And what are they able they do? In this free webinar, we hear from representatives of both the UK and Chile's overseers.

We hope you'll join us on Sept 28: find out more and book here.

Christian is Head of the Training and Promotion Unit at Consejo para la Transparencia (Council of Transparency), Chile’s equivalent of the ICO.

In this role, he conceives and oversees training initiatives, outreach and educational programmes.

Aiden, from the UK's Information Commissioner’s Office, is Senior Upstream Regulation Officer in their FOI and Transparency division.

This team works to proactively prevent breaches of the FOI Act and the Environmental Information Regulations.

title: Access To Information in practice
content:
Dear friend,

Join us for one or more of our three webinars this autumn, where you’ll hear practical experiences of delivering, defending and building Access to Information.

Across these sessions, we’ll hear how regulators in the UK and Chile can help people exercise their rights; how civil society in Germany and Mexico is responding to threats and changes to FOI; and what we can learn from building ATI infrastructure in Peru and across Europe.

The series is designed as a space for practical learning and exchange between anyone with an interest in the right to information. It all kicks off on 28 September, International Right to Know Day!

Find out more and book here.

Aiden Clarkson from the UK’s ICO and Christian Anker from Chile’s Council of Transparency discuss what good regulatory support looks like in practice. Find out more and book here.

Veza Clute-Simon and Martin Szyszlican will share what has been happening in their respective countries — and how civil society has responded.

title: TICTeC presents: Digital Democracy Edinburgh
content:
Here’s something to look forward to in 2027! Put the date in your diary now, and get set to join us in one of the UK’s most beautiful cities, for two days of exploring how digital tools can help make democratic systems more effective, inclusive and participatory.

Bringing together international approaches as well as local innovation from Scotland and across the UK, the conference will showcase and connect some of the most exciting thinking and practice in digital democracy.

We’ll share details of registration, and an open call for proposals, in the next few weeks, with opportunities for researchers, practitioners and others working across these areas to contribute to the programme.

But for now, put 11-12 March 2027 in your calendar, and sign up for updates to hear when further details are announced.

title: They work for you (and we do too)
content:
Dear friend,

Here’s what we’ve been doing recently to make that happen. 

Our alerts service will send you an email whenever your chosen keyword or phrase is mentioned in Parliament; or you can follow any MP or other representative to receive an email when they speak or vote.

So far in 2026, we’ve sent 2.2 million email alerts and our users have created almost 2,000 new keyword alerts through our new and improved alerts management system.

This service helps people understand what their representatives (across all of the UK’s Parliaments) are saying and doing, and also provides an essential service in providing free parliamentary monitoring to civic groups and organisations who can now have as much access to this intel as those with big pockets.

This doesn’t happen by itself: every day our team pulls together the transcripts from the UK's Parliaments, fixing formatting issues and broken files to get these loaded into the site and our alerts.

If you don’t have alerts set up, what are you waiting for? You can do it now at TheyWorkForYou.com.

title: Watching 'Buried' with Michael Sheen?
content:
Dear friend,

Have you watched the BBC two-parter Buried, in which actor Michael Sheen follows the evidence around several toxic waste dumps across Wales and England? 

We were very interested to learn that much of the research that informed the programme was obtained via our Freedom of Information site, WhatDoTheyKnow, by a tireless campaigner for the truth — vicar Paul Cawthorne.

We spoke to Paul to learn more about the part FOI has played in bringing this terrible scandal to public attention. Read our conversation here.

This isn’t the first time our sites have played a part in a TV campaign. In October 2023, we spoke to WhatDoTheyKnow user Eleanor Shaikh, who’d uncovered crucial evidence about the Post Office scandal.

In January ’24, the extent of the issue hit the public consciousness via TV series Mr Bates vs the Post Office. You can hear Eleanor explain how she used FOI in this ten minute podcast.

And all the way back in 2011, we built the app for George Martin’s empty homes campaign, the Great British Property Scandal.

That programme is now off air, but you can read more about how we adapted our FixMyStreet codebase so people could report empty buildings in their area.
